name: Bleeding Diathesis Due to a Collagen Receptor Defect

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Collagen Receptor Defect Bleeding Disorder Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Recurrent mucocutaneous bleeding including easy bruising and epistaxis
Impaired platelet aggregation response to collagen in platelet function assays
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes encoding platelet collagen receptors (e.g., GP6, ITGA2)
Normal coagulation factor levels and normal prothrombin time (PT) and activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT)
Positive family history of similar bleeding symptoms consistent with autosomal recessive or dominant inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of recurrent mucocutaneous bleeding, impaired platelet aggregation to collagen, and identification of pathogenic collagen receptor gene variants
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other platelet function disorders and coagulation factor deficiencies.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Impaired platelet aggregation response to collagen
searchTerms: platelets don't clump well with collagen
poor platelet clumping response to collagen

pathognomonic.notes: Includes frequent epistaxis and gingival bleeding
searchTerms: frequent bleeding from skin and mucous membranes
repeated bleeding from mouth and skin

common.symptomName: Prolonged bleeding after minor cuts or dental procedures
searchTerms: bleeding longer after small cuts or dental work

occasional.notes: Less common than in coagulation factor deficiencies
May present as melena or hematochezia

rare.notes: Microscopic or gross blood in urine

laboratory: Impaired platelet aggregation response to collagen in platelet function tests
Normal platelet count with functional defects
imaging: Imaging may reveal hemorrhagic complications such as intracranial bleeding or hemarthrosis
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes encoding platelet collagen receptors (e.g., GP6, ITGA2)
Autosomal recessive or dominant inheritance patterns
other: Family history consistent with inherited platelet function disorder
Bleeding severity disproportionate to platelet count

distinguishingFeatures: Defect in platelet integrin αIIbβ3 rather than collagen receptor
Absent platelet aggregation with multiple agonists including ADP and thrombin
Defect in platelet glycoprotein Ib-IX-V complex
Impaired platelet adhesion to von Willebrand factor

redFlags: Severe mucocutaneous bleeding unresponsive to local measures
Intracranial hemorrhage or other life-threatening bleeding
Bleeding disproportionate to platelet count or coagulation studies
references: Nurden AT. Platelet collagen receptors. Thromb Haemost. 2007;98(1):1-9.
Kunicki TJ, Nugent DJ. Platelet collagen receptor defects: clinical and molecular aspects. Blood Rev. 2000;14(3):139-148.
Orphanet: Bleeding diathesis due to a collagen receptor defect. ORPHA:73271.
